In the vulnerable 1.7.3, isAbsoluteURL/http.js treat the protocol-relative path as absolute and attempt a genuine DNS lookup against the attacker hostname (surfacing as ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN referencing that hostname), proving the request escaped baseURL scoping — this is classified as exploit_succeeded=true. No sockets are opened by the oracle itself; all network behavior originates from axios's own adapter, and failures are distinguished purely by inspecting the genuine error codes/addresses/hostnames axios surfaces, without reimplementing or hardcoding the patch's literal error string.
